note: Second domestic cup (league cup / regional cup) per country. One representative season each; where the competition no longer runs the last edition or the abolition is recorded. Format values: single_leg_knockout, group_stage_then_knockout, none.

competitions.name: EFL Cup (Carabao Cup)
competitions.participants: all 92 Premier League and EFL clubs (20 PL, 24 Championship, 24 League One, 24 League Two); a 4-club preliminary round is played when European entrants force it
competitions.quote: All 92 clubs in the Premier League and English Football League entered the season's EFL Cup.
competitions.winner_quote: The winner of the competition (Manchester City) qualified for the play-off round of the 2026-27 UEFA Conference League.
competitions.note: Round 1 proper week of 11 August; a 4-club preliminary round was played 29 July - 5 August (newly promoted + two lowest non-relegated League Two clubs). Semi-finals are the only two-legged round (12 Jan and 2 Feb legs).

competitions.name: Scottish League Cup (Premier Sports Cup)
competitions.participants: 45 clubs: 40 in the group stage (all remaining SPFL clubs + Highland League champions/runners-up + Lowland League champions); the 5 UEFA entrants (Celtic, Rangers, Aberdeen, Hibernian, Dundee United) enter at the second round
competitions.winner_gets: nothing (no European berth; Scottish Cup winner takes the Europa League place)
competitions.quote: The competition began with eight groups of five teams.
competitions.winner_quote: the 80th season of Scotland's second-most prestigious football knockout competition
competitions.note: 8 groups of 5, single round-robin, 3 pts win / 1 pt draw plus a bonus point for winning the penalty shoot-out in a drawn group match. 8 group winners + 3 best runners-up + 5 UEFA byes = last 16; knockout is single leg, final at a neutral venue (Hampden).

competitions.name: Taça da Liga (Allianz Cup)
competitions.participants: 8 clubs: top six of the Primeira Liga + top two non-reserve clubs of Liga Portugal 2
competitions.quote: the top six teams from the Primeira Liga and the top two non-reserve teams from the Liga Portugal 2 were paired according to their league positions to play single-leg quarter-final matches
competitions.note: No group stage in 2025-26: 8 clubs, single-leg quarter-finals at the higher-ranked club's ground, then a 4-team final four (2 semi-finals + final) at a neutral venue in Leiria. The group stage existed in earlier editions (up to 2023-24); the field was cut to 8 from 2024-25. European places come from the Primeira Liga and the Taça de Portugal, not this cup.

competitions.name: Coupe de la Ligue
competitions.participants: 42 professional clubs (Ligue 1, Ligue 2, National) in its last format
competitions.quote: The LFP suspended the competition indefinitely after the 2019-20 season, to reduce fixture congestion.
competitions.note: Ran 1994-95 to 2019-20; last final played 31 July 2020 (PSG beat Lyon on penalties). A UEFA Europa League berth went to the winner for most of its history. France now has only the Coupe de France (plus the Trophée des Champions).

competitions.name: Copa de la Liga Profesional
competitions.participants: all Primera División clubs (28 in 2024), drawn into two zones
competitions.winner_gets: none (competition abolished; it gave a Copa Libertadores berth while it ran)
competitions.quote: The Copa de la Liga Profesional (English: Professional League Cup ...) was an official Argentine football cup competition.
competitions.note: Infobox records 'Abolished 2025'; last champion Estudiantes (LP) in 2024. Format was group stage (2 zones, single round-robin) + knockout final, not a straight cup. The 2025 season was restructured into Apertura/Clausura league tournaments and the cup was dropped; Argentina now has only the Copa Argentina (plus Supercopa Argentina / Trofeo de Campeones).

competitions.name: Copa MX
competitions.participants: 24-27 clubs: Liga MX clubs not in CONCACAF competition + Ascenso MX clubs
competitions.winner_gets: none (competition abolished; winner got a Supercopa MX place until 2019)
competitions.quote: After the 2019-20 edition, the competition was abolished due to busy calendar issues with the FMF giving preference to matches of the Mexico national team in preparation to the 2022 FIFA World Cup.
competitions.note: Infobox: abolished 2020. Its last format was group stage (8-9 groups of 3) + single-elimination knockout. Mexico keeps only the Campeón de Campeones super cup.

competitions.name: J.League Cup (YBC Levain Cup)
competitions.participants: 60 clubs: every J1, J2 and J3 club
competitions.quote: All clubs from the 2025 season's J1, J2, and J3 League participated.
competitions.note: Not a table group stage: 55 clubs are split into 7 groups of 8 playing 3 single-leg knockout rounds; 7 winners + 1 bye join the play-off round (two legs), then a prime round of QF and SF (two legs) and a single-leg final at a neutral venue. The 4 AFC/Club World Cup clubs and the ACL Two quarter-finalist enter only at the prime round. Second season with all 60 clubs.

competitions.name: Copa do Nordeste
competitions.participants: 16 clubs from the 9 Northeast states (state champions + best-placed clubs by CBF ranking + 4 qualifiers from a pre-tournament)
competitions.winner_gets: berth in the third round of the 2026 Copa do Brasil
competitions.quote: The competition featured 16 clubs, with Bahia, Ceará and Pernambuco having two seeds each, and Alagoas, Maranhão, Paraíba, Piauí, Rio Grande do Norte and Sergipe with one seed each.
competitions.note: Two groups of 8, single round-robin; top 4 of each to QF/SF (single leg, higher seed at home); final home-and-away. Regional cup, not a national league cup - it runs alongside the Copa do Brasil.

competitions.name: Copa Verde
competitions.participants: 24 clubs from 12 states of the North, Central-West and Espírito Santo plus the Federal District (state champions/runners-up + CBF-ranking berths)
competitions.winner_gets: berth in the third round of the 2026 Copa do Brasil
competitions.quote: In the finals, Paysandu defeated Goiás 5-4 on penalties after tied 1-1 on aggregate to win their 5th title and a place in the third round of the 2026 Copa do Brasil.
competitions.note: Round 1 and round of 16 single leg; QF, SF and final home-and-away. 2025 was the last edition in tournament format - from 2026 it becomes a supercup between the Copa Verde and Copa do Nordeste winners / state champions.

competitions.name: no second cup
competitions.quote: Due to time constraints, saturation and club pressure, the competition only lasted four years, being cancelled in 1986.
competitions.note: Only the Copa del Rey + Supercopa de España. The Copa de la Liga ran 1982-86 (all ties two-legged) and was never revived. The Copa Federación is a separate cup for Segunda RFEF/Tercera clubs, not a second top-flight cup.

competitions.name: no second cup
competitions.quote: Coppa Italia Serie C, formerly named Coppa Italia Lega Pro, is a straight knock-out based competition involving teams from Serie C in Italian football first held in 1972.
competitions.note: Serie A has only the Coppa Italia + Supercoppa Italiana. Coppa Italia Serie C is a separate cup restricted to tier-3 clubs (and Coppa Italia Dilettanti to amateurs), so there is no second cup a Serie A club can enter.

competitions.name: no second cup
competitions.quote: The Ligapokal was not held in 2009 either, due to the German Football Association's decision to abolish it.
competitions.note: Only the DFB-Pokal + DFL-Supercup. The DFL-Ligapokal (6 clubs, pre-season, top 4 Bundesliga + cup winner + 2. Bundesliga winner) ran 1997-2007 and was abolished; no replacement second cup.

competitions.name: Northern Ireland Football League Cup (BetMcLean Cup)
competitions.participants: 38 NIFL clubs: 12 NIFL Premiership, 12 NIFL Championship, 14 NIFL Premier Intermediate League
competitions.quote: Unlike the Irish Cup, the League Cup does not have a berth for UEFA Conference League qualification.
competitions.note: All ties single leg with extra time + penalties, no replays. 14 Premier Intermediate clubs play a preliminary round; the 16 highest-ranked clubs are seeded only in round 1. Third-most prestigious domestic competition after the Premiership and the Irish Cup. The County Antrim Shield is a regional (County Antrim FA) cup, not a national one.

competitions.name: Cymru League Cup (Nathaniel MG Cup)
competitions.participants: 44 clubs: 12 Cymru Premier + Cymru North + Cymru South, plus Cardiff City and Swansea City U21 wildcards
competitions.winner_gets: Scottish Challenge Cup berth (no European berth)
competitions.quote: 44 clubs in the Cymru Premier, Cymru North and Cymru South leagues entered the season's League Cup.
competitions.note: Single leg throughout; draw regionalised (north/south) up to the semi-finals; Cymru Premier clubs get a bye to round 2. Winner's Scottish Challenge Cup place comes from the 2019-20 agreement and was not re-verified for 2025-26. FAW confirmed the competition will NOT be played in 2026-27 (Cymru Premier expansion, fixture load). A 2024-25 proposal to give the winner a UEFA Conference League place and admit the four Welsh EFL clubs was rejected by the English FA in January 2025.

competitions.name: Durand Cup
competitions.participants: 24 clubs: 6 Indian Super League, 4 I-League, 2 I-League 2, 5 state-league, 5 armed-forces teams + 2 invited foreign army teams
competitions.quote: the 134th edition of the Durand Cup, the oldest football tournament in Asia
competitions.note: 6 groups + QF/SF/final single leg (draws decided straight on penalties). India is one of the countries with two national cups: the Durand Cup (July-August) and the AIFF Super Cup (formerly Kalinga Super Cup) - both open to ISL and I-League clubs.

competitions.name: Carling Knockout Cup
competitions.participants: 16 clubs: all clubs of the Premiership
competitions.quote: The teams consisted of the 16 teams from the 2025-26 South African Premiership.
competitions.note: Round of 16 to final, all single leg with extra time + penalties. South Africa runs three cups: Nedbank Cup (open to all tiers, the main cup), MTN 8 (top 8 of the Premiership, Aug-Oct) and Carling Knockout (16 Premiership clubs, Oct-Dec).

competitions.name: Toto Cup Al
competitions.participants: 14 clubs: all Israeli Premier League clubs; a separate Toto Cup Leumit runs for the 16 Liga Leumit clubs
competitions.winner_gets: prize money only (NIS 1.25m; no European berth)
competitions.quote: the 41st season of the football tournament in Israel since its introduction and the 19th tournament involving Israeli Premier League clubs only
competitions.note: The 4 UEFA-entrant clubs skip the group stage and enter through play-in matches (Super Cup / UEFA-qualifier match); the other 10 play two groups of 5 by geography. Group winners + 2 play-in winners make the semi-finals; all 14 clubs then play classification matches for places 5-14. The cup is per division (Al / Leumit), so two separate Toto Cups run in parallel.
